goals.goal: Before engaging the external payment provider as a sub-processor, the controller verifies that the provider offers sufficient guarantees to implement appropriate technical and organisational measures so that processing meets GDPR requirements and protects data-subject rights; the Art. 28(3) closed-list DPA clauses (a)–(h) are documented in the processor contract and the Art. 28(2) sub-processor authorisation chain is maintained in the Art. 30(2) RoPA processor record.
goals.adjustment: Proportionally scoped to the single external payment-provider sub-processor relationship at 8-employee SaaS scale; the EDPB Guidelines 07/2020 4-factor assessment operationalises the qualitative `sufficient guarantees` threshold for that one processor engagement rather than a multi-processor portfolio.

goals.goal: When integrating components sourced from third parties — including components of free and open-source software not made available on the market in the course of a commercial activity — the manufacturer exercises due diligence (procedural and substantive) so that those components do not compromise the cybersecurity of the product with digital elements; on becoming aware of a component vulnerability, the manufacturer addresses and remediates it without delay and shares relevant information with the component supplier.
goals.adjustment: Proportionally scoped to the self-assessment-class SaaS platform's third-party component set (commercial libraries and non-commercial OSS) at 8-employee manufacturer scale; the R3 procedural + substantive due-diligence reading applies with OSS-specific calibration (stewardship, CVD policy, vulnerability-disclosure channel) rather than a multi-tier enterprise supply-chain programme.
